comment: Why: the Holy road is a tower of light, so almost every party in it is bright (block light at the eyes, torches in hand) and the light modifier of the dice would make encounters likelier than on any dim floor; the roll bonus of minus two cancels most of that, so a bright party is met about as often as a dim one elsewhere. The monsters are what a holy tower keeps: gilded armour and golems (the construct tag), choirs and priests (the cultist tag), spirits (the elemental tag) and the conjured lights of the Rukh (vexes, owls). Entries that need light are common here and the one that needs the dark is rare, because a party in the dark is the exception on this road: it is the intruder, and what finds it is a stain of the dead.
description: The Holy road: white quartz, smooth stone, gold and calcite, light in every room and the air thick with Light Rukh. Golden armour, choirs and conjured lights keep a tower that wants to be climbed; here the dark is the intruder.

entries.comment: The breather of the tower: one or two of the room's own people (the construct tag unless the room has a native faction). No upper threat, so the minor band never runs dry.
Motes of the Light Rukh made flesh: a couple of vexes drawn to a bright party. On this road the party is nearly always bright, so this is the common nuisance.
The evergreen standard encounter: the tower's gilded armour on its rounds. The id is explicit so the first floors, where the construct tag is thin, still have a reliable fight.
The Rukh as birds: owls with a conjured light or two among them, drawn to a bright party. The vexes are trimmed first when the budget is short.
The caster pair of the tower: a choir of the cultist tag with the tower's constructs for guards. Casters first, so the entry always has them; the guards are trimmed first when the budget is short.
Spirits and winds of the elemental tag, drawn to a lit party. The tag decides who comes (breezes, Tensura's spirits and the rest within the toughness window).

Turrets in the wall: shulkers do not move, so they are placed close and never sent hunting (hunt 0); the party meets them by walking into their range. In a tower of light they are the windows that watch.
Light is an illusionist's medium: for a bright party, an illusioner (blindness and mirror images) with conjured lights for company.

The rare dark entry of this road: a party that has put its lights out, or lost them, is a stain in the tower and what finds it is the dead who climbed and did not arrive. One or two, never scaled by the party.

The loud brute: the tower's golem (100 health, five points of budget) wakes to a noisy party, as a bell wakes a chapter. One body, a lot of health; hard band only and from threat 3, where a hard budget can pay for it.
The mimic-style surprise: the golden armour in the niche steps out, an evoker at its shoulder. Close range and a short hunt, because the point is that it was always there.
The tower's inquisitors for a party that shines: casters first (two kinds, so the fight has two tricks), the tower's constructs as bodyguards.
The wave of the tower: a horn, and the light itself comes for the party, many conjured lights in three places and a priest behind them.
The late ambush: golems and gilded armour in procession, from two sides. Only for parties of two or more.
